title: How the rosary is built
hookLine: the creed, an Our Father, three Hail Marys, then five decades each on one mystery

cards: A string of beads wrapped around a rearview mirror. Wound around a grandmother's fingers in a hospital bed. Tucked in a soldier's pocket.
Dangling from a teenager's wrist. Laid in the hands of someone in a coffin. Hang around Catholics long enough and you'll see them.
You met the beads back on day four. This week, i'll open the rosary up, bead by bead, and show what people are thinking about while their fingers move. It's built like a small machine for prayer.
Today's word is its main part.

teach.b: Start at the cross that hangs from the end. Holding it, you make the sign of the cross and say the Apostles' Creed, the one from day one hundred and one. Moving up, one big bead: an Our Father.
Three small beads: three Hail Marys, traditionally for faith, hope and love. Then a Glory Be. That's the doorway.
Now the circle: five groups of ten small beads, each marked off by one bigger bead. Each group of ten is a decade, from the Greek and Latin for ten.
For each decade, you name a mystery, a moment from the lives of Jesus and Mary, then pray one Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be.
The Hail Mary's first half is from Luke, in the Douay-Rheims: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women." and "blessed is the fruit of thy womb."
The second half asks Mary to pray for us, now and at the hour of our death.

teach.h: LIPS SAY, MIND STAYS IN THE SCENE.
teach.b: Catholics describe it this way: the words make a rhythm, and while the lips say the Hail Mary, the mind stays in the scene.
The name rosary comes from the Latin rosarium, a rose garden: each Hail Mary like a rose, offered.

teach.h: HAIL, FULL OF GRACE, THE LORD IS WITH THEE.
teach.b: There's an old story that Mary gave the rosary to Saint Dominic. Historians see it growing slowly, over a long time. Either way, in 1569 Pope Pius the Fifth wrote it down in a form close to the one prayed today.

how: Catholics pray the rosary alone or in groups, often daily: the sign of the cross and the Apostles' Creed on the crucifix, an Our Father, three Hail Marys and a Glory Be, then five decades, each an Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be while meditating on one mystery, often ending with the Hail, Holy Queen.

name a mystery, then pray an Our Father.
games.why: each decade begins by naming a mystery, a moment from the lives of Jesus and Mary, then an Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be.

practice: Take the rosary's doorway one slow breath at a time, holding the cross if you have beads, or your thumb if not: one breath for the cross, one for the big bead, three for faith, hope and love, one for the Glory Be, six in all.
If you pray, say the prayers instead, one on each; if you don't, let each breath stand for one bead. Then rest at the edge of the circle, in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Decade. A group of ten beads on the rosary, and ten Hail Marys prayed on one mystery. Five make a rosary. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: a rose garden, the root of rosary.

carryVoice: Your line: a garden of roses. Five decades, one mystery each, all on one string of beads. See you tomorrow.
